message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $3611 and a pink monopoly with hotels. The opponent has only $29 and mostly mortgaged properties. I am considering whether to trade or build.

The opponent just passed GO and built a house on Boardwalk. They now have $29 cash, 3 houses on Park Place, and 4 houses on Boardwalk.

I can afford the rent on both dark blues. I am now checking board positions.

I am mapping the board positions to identify which Community Chest I am on. I was on Pacific in turn 214, and turns 215 and 216 were taken by the opponent.

Turn 217 is my turn. I have already moved and landed on a Community Chest space.

I am weighing four post-turn options: ending the turn, proposing a trade with p1, unmortgaging the railroad or Tennessee Avenue, or selling houses on the pink properties. I have decided not to sell hotels, since they are the most powerful asset.

Unmortgaging the railroad or Tennessee Avenue is not worthwhile. I will keep my get-out-of-jail-free cards and avoid trading cash, jail passes, or pink properties.

I am now calculating whether the opponent can survive a pink hotel rent. They would need to sell houses at half price to pay the $750–$900 rent.

The opponent can liquidate at most $779 by selling houses and mortgaging Vermont. They can barely pay the $750 rent on St. Charles or States hotels, but they cannot afford the $900 rent on Virginia hotel. That is the kill shot.

The opponent is on GO. From there, the maximum roll is 12, so they cannot land on States or Virginia in one turn. They can only reach St. Charles Place with an 11. That hotel rent is $750, which they can afford by liquidating their houses and Vermont.

The probability of rolling an 11 is only about 5.6%, so the opponent will most likely avoid the pink hotels next turn. From GO, their path passes through several other spaces before reaching St. Charles Place.

I am checking whether mortgaged properties still count for light-blue monopoly rent doubling. If they do not, the opponent would face no rent on Vermont from GO.

Mortgaged properties still count for light-blue monopoly rent doubling. Vermont would cost only $12.

The Community Chest I am on determines the next roll. If it is between St. James and Tennessee, I pass their mortgaged oranges with no rent. If it is between North Carolina and Pennsylvania, I could land on Park Place or Boardwalk.

I am tracing the board from Pacific to identify which Community Chest I landed on. A roll of three spaces from Pacific would reach the chest before Pennsylvania Avenue. From there, four spaces forward lands on Park Place.

I am now on the Community Chest between North Carolina and Pennsylvania. A roll of four spaces lands on Park Place, and a roll of six lands on Boardwalk. Both are affordable.

This is a post-turn decision, so the movement and rent danger are already resolved. I am checking why my cash dropped from $3966 to $3611. Likely causes are luxury tax, income tax, or rent.

The $355 gap is not a standard rent amount. I am now considering whether a Chance card or another action already occurred this turn before the post-turn decision.

I checked the general repairs tax. Three hotels cost $300 or $345, neither matching the $355 drop. The cash difference likely came from rent or another action. I am also reconsidering whether a broken color group affects Vermont rent.

Standard rules confirm that a mortgaged property breaks the light-blue monopoly, so Vermont rent is only $6. That does not explain the $355 cash drop. I checked whether I landed on Boardwalk or Park Place, but both would leave me with roughly $2200–$2800, not $3611. The earlier $3966 figure was likely just a note; the authoritative game state shows $3611. I can easily afford both dark-blue hotels.

I am now calculating the exact return from selling a hotel. The bank has 25 houses available, so I could downgrade to four houses and recover half the hotel cost. This would drop rent significantly, but I am still deciding whether that trade-off is worthwhile.

Selling the Virginia hotel would drop rent to $750, which the opponent can afford. That removes the guaranteed kill shot, so selling hotels is a clear mistake. Unmortgaging the railroad is also unwise because the rent would fall to $25 and the cost is too high.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue is also pointless. It costs $99 to unmortgage and would only yield a single red property worth $14 in rent. Trading it would complete the opponent's orange monopoly, so I will keep it mortgaged. I am now considering whether to trade for their Park Place or Boardwalk.

I will not trade for the opponent's dark-blue properties. They would never give up their only weapon, and giving them cash would let them build hotels on those spaces. Boardwalk is currently at four houses, so they cannot upgrade it until they raise cash. I still own the mortgaged Tennessee Avenue.

I cannot trade for the opponent's dark-blue properties. They would never sell them, and any offer that gives them cash or my pink hotels would backfire. I will not trade.

I will keep both get-out-of-jail-free cards. The opponent has none, and rolling doubles from jail would land them on St. Charles or Virginia hotels. I am ending the turn.

I will keep the "Passing" message consistent. The opponent has $29 and three houses on the dark blues, but they still need $200 to build the fourth house or hotel. They just spent their GO money on a house, so they cannot upgrade immediately.
